executive_summary.narrative: The web application has multiple critical vulnerabilities, including SQL injection and authentication bypass, but none were proven due to time constraints; they are hypotheses that need validation. The risk posture is high if these exist, as attackers could gain full control. Prioritize fixing the unauthenticated SQLi (W-002) and authentication bypass (W-003) first, as they may allow complete compromise. Then address the IDORs and access control issues (W-005, W-006, W-010, W-012). Confidence in findings is moderate: they are based on static analysis and manual inspection, but not active exploitation; further testing is advised to confirm before claiming confirmed risk.

findings.title: Potential SQL injection in /rest/products
findings.status: tested, not proven (HTTP 500: an error page is not evidence of this flaw)
findings.recommendation: Parameterize all SQL queries in the /rest/products endpoint. Specifically, refactor the product search/list functions to use prepared statements or an ORM with bound parameters. Add a WAF rule to block suspicious SQL patterns as a defense-in-depth measure.

evidence.note: Asset confirmed reachable. This evidences existence, not exploitability.
If the response contains an SQL error message, the product search is vulnerable to SQL injection.

findings.title: Authentication bypass in /rest/user/login
findings.recommendation: Review the authentication logic in /rest/user/login; it likely has a flaw in session handling or token verification. Ensure the token is cryptographically signed, not predictable, and validated on every request. Implement multi-factor authentication to mitigate bypass attempts.

evidence.note: Asset confirmed reachable. This evidences existence, not exploitability.

findings.title: Unrestricted file upload at /file-upload
findings.status: tested, not proven (request error: request failed: )
findings.recommendation: On the /file-upload endpoint, implement strict file type validation based on magic bytes (not just MIME), restrict allowed extensions, and store uploaded files outside the web root with random filenames. Also ensure the upload directory has execute permissions disabled and use a content security policy to prevent execution of uploaded scripts.

findings.status: tested, not proven (HTTP 500: an error page is not evidence of this flaw)

findings.title: Insecure direct object reference on /api/Users/{id}
findings.status: tested, not proven (signal 'email' did not appear in the response)
findings.recommendation: On the /api/Users/{id} endpoint, enforce authorization checks that verify the requesting user has permission to access the specific user ID. Use session-based access control and validate the ID belongs to the authenticated user or role. Avoid relying on client-supplied IDs alone.

evidence.note: Asset confirmed reachable. This evidences existence, not exploitability.
If an unauthenticated request to a specific user ID returns that user's email, the IDOR is proven.

findings.title: IDOR on /api/BasketItems (own basket vs others)
findings.recommendation: In /api/BasketItems, enforce that users can only access their own basket items. Add ownership checks based on the authenticated user's session, and validate that the basket ID belongs to that user. Consider using a GUID instead of sequential IDs and implement proper authorization.

evidence.note: Asset confirmed reachable. This evidences existence, not exploitability.

findings.title: Admin functionality exposed without proper auth at /rest/admin
findings.recommendation: Restrict access to /rest/admin and all admin endpoints with role-based authorization. Implement a middleware that checks the user's role for admin-only routes. Additionally, ensure admin functions are not accessible via direct URL without proper session and CSRF token validation.

evidence.note: Asset confirmed reachable. This evidences existence, not exploitability.
If the admin endpoint is accessible without authentication and returns 200, admin functionality is exposed.

findings.title: Information disclosure via /rest/admin/application-configuration
findings.status: tested, not proven (signal 'config' is present without the payload too, so it demonstrates nothing)
findings.recommendation: Remove or restrict the /rest/admin/application-configuration endpoint to authorized admins only. If it must exist, require authentication and role checks, and mask sensitive values (e.g., passwords, API keys) in responses. Audit logs should be enabled to monitor access.

findings.status: tested, not proven (signal 'email' did not appear in the response)

findings.recommendation: Review /rest/user/authentication-details; do not expose authentication details (e.g., password hashes, tokens) in API responses. Remove the endpoint or restrict it to admins and mask sensitive fields. If needed for debugging, log but never return in the response.

findings.title: Reflected XSS via search query in /search
findings.status: tested, not proven (signal "<script>alert('reflected')</script>" did not appear in the response)
findings.recommendation: For the /search endpoint, URL-encode and HTML-encode the search query before reflecting it in the response. Use a secure output encoding function like OWASP's ESAPI. Additionally, set the X-XSS-Protection header and implement a strict CSP.

findings.title: User enumeration via /api/Users response differences
findings.status: tested, not proven (signal 'email' did not appear in the response)
findings.recommendation: Modify the /api/Users endpoint to return identical generic responses for both existing and non-existing users. Remove any differences in status codes, response times, or error messages. Implement rate limiting to slow down enumeration attempts.

evidence.note: Asset confirmed reachable. This evidences existence, not exploitability.

caveats: Produced by an autonomous pipeline with no human review. Findings should be validated by a security engineer before remediation is prioritised or the results are shared externally.
API routes were extracted from client-side JavaScript. They are candidate routes the application references, not a verified inventory of its endpoints.
12 of 12 findings were not proven exploitable (W-002, W-003, W-001, W-008, W-005, W-012, W-006, W-007, …). They are hypotheses based on observed assets, not demonstrated vulnerabilities.
2 findings were never tested for exploitability (W-011, W-012). No claim is made about them either way.
Absence of a finding is not evidence of absence. This engagement covered what the crawler reached within its configured bounds.
